title: Your Coffee Is Still Awake

pre.en: By what time do most experts say you should stop drinking coffee?
pre.zh: 大多数专家建议几点以后就别再喝咖啡了？

intro: 一期电台节目：听众 Nadia 来信问，为什么下午那杯咖啡会让人半夜睡不着？主持人先讲道理，再讲 Nadia 后来的经历，最后给建议。读的时候留意现在完成进行时 have been doing：从过去一直持续到现在的事，比如「好几个星期都睡不好」。结尾和听众开了个玩笑。

sentences.en: This week's question comes from a listener called Nadia.
sentences.zh: 这周的问题来自一位叫 Nadia 的听众。

sentences.en: "I'm writing to ask a simple question," she said in her email.
sentences.zh: 她在邮件里说：「我写信是想问个简单的问题。」

sentences.en: "I've been sleeping badly for weeks, and I keep waking up at three."
sentences.zh: 「我已经好几个星期没睡好了，老是凌晨三点就醒。」

sentences.en: "Is it my coffee?"
sentences.zh: 「是咖啡闹的吗？」

sentences.en: Nadia's twenty-nine, she works in marketing, and she drinks four cups a day.
sentences.zh: Nadia 二十九岁，做市场营销，一天喝四杯咖啡。

sentences.en: Whenever her boss emails her late in the afternoon, she says "I'm on it" and makes another flat white.
sentences.zh: 每次老板快下班了还发邮件派活儿，她就回一句「马上办」，然后再冲一杯馥芮白。

sentences.en: Well, Nadia, that's a good question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，Nadia，这个问题问得好。

sentences.en: It's a long story, but here's the short version.
sentences.zh: 说来话长，我给你讲个简短版。

sentences.en: Caffeine usually kicks in about twenty minutes after your first cup.
sentences.zh: 第一杯咖啡下肚，大概二十分钟，咖啡因就开始起作用了。

sentences.en: At nine in the morning, that first cup brings the whole office to life.
sentences.zh: 早上九点，就是这第一杯，让整个办公室都活过来了。

sentences.en: The problem is, it takes five or six hours for just half of it to wear off.
sentences.zh: 问题是，光是让一半的咖啡因消退，就得五六个小时。

sentences.en: So a flat white at four is still keeping you awake at midnight.
sentences.zh: 所以下午四点那杯馥芮白，到半夜还在让你睡不着。

sentences.en: Sleep researchers have been studying this for years, and one survey after another shows the same pattern.
sentences.zh: 睡眠研究人员研究这个问题已经很多年了，一次次调查都显示出同一个规律。

sentences.en: Lots of people rely on coffee to get through the afternoon.
sentences.zh: 很多人下午全靠咖啡撑着。

sentences.en: And those people find it harder to get a good night's sleep.
sentences.zh: 而这些人晚上更难睡个好觉。

sentences.en: The next morning they're tired, so they drink more, and the habit slowly builds up.
sentences.zh: 第二天早上一累，就喝得更多，这个习惯就这么一点点加重了。

sentences.en: Nadia emailed us again yesterday.
sentences.zh: Nadia 昨天又给我们发了封邮件。

sentences.en: She decided to bring it up with her doctor.
sentences.zh: 她决定跟医生说说这事。

sentences.en: He asked her just one question: "How long have you been drinking coffee after lunch?"
sentences.zh: 医生只问了她一个问题：「你午饭后喝咖啡有多久了？」

sentences.en: "Since I started this job," she said.
sentences.zh: 「从我干这份工作开始，」她说。

sentences.en: So, most experts say you should have a coffee cut-off at two o'clock.
sentences.zh: 所以，大多数专家建议，下午两点以后就别再喝咖啡了。

sentences.en: And when you first wake up, have a glass of water.
sentences.zh: 早上刚醒的时候，先喝一杯水。

sentences.en: Nadia tried it, and after a week she stopped waking up at three.
sentences.zh: Nadia 试了一下，一个星期后就不再凌晨三点醒了。

sentences.en: She also skips her afternoon coffees now, which has freed up about ten pounds a week.
sentences.zh: 她现在下午也不喝咖啡了，每周还因此省下差不多 10 英镑。

sentences.en: Oh, and if you've been listening to this at eleven at night with a latte in your hand...
sentences.zh: 对了，要是你正在晚上十一点、手里端着一杯拿铁听这期节目……

sentences.en: Well, at least you won't miss the end.
sentences.zh: 嗯，至少你不会错过结尾。

cards.zh: 来信是想……（邮件开头说明目的）
cards.note: used at the start of an email or letter to say why you are writing
cards.tip: 后面接动词原形：I'm writing to ask / to complain / to confirm。
cards.example: I'm writing to ask about the job you advertised.

cards.note: 说在哪个行业工作用 work in：work in IT / work in marketing。
used to say that you have started dealing with a problem or task

cards.zh: 问得好（常用来争取时间或回避）
cards.note: something you say when you need time to think, or when you do not know the answer
said when something is too complicated to explain now, or you do not want to explain it
cards.tip: 常用来不想细说时打个岔；也可以接 but：It's a long story, but…
cards.example: Why am I wearing my dad's coat? It's a long story.

cards.note: the short version 是「简短的说法」；软件的新版本是 the new version。
读 /ˈkæfiːn/，不可数。茶、可乐、巧克力里也有。
to start to have an effect
cards.tip: 常说药、咖啡、新规定等开始起效；不用被动。
cards.example: Take the medicine now — it takes about an hour to kick in.

cards.note: to make something more interesting or exciting
cards.tip: bring 的过去式是 brought；come to life 是「活跃起来」，不带宾语。
cards.example: The music really brought the party to life.

cards.note: to gradually stop having an effect
cards.tip: 和 kick in 正好相反；wear 的过去式 wore，过去分词 worn。
cards.example: The excitement wore off after the first week.

cards.note: to stop someone from falling asleep
cards.tip: keep + 人 + 形容词，说让人保持某种状态：keep sb warm / keep sb busy。
cards.example: The noise from the party kept us awake all night.

cards.note: research（研究）加 -er；research 不可数，不说 a research。
也指图案：a shirt with a flower pattern。
to need something or someone in order to do something
cards.tip: 介词固定用 on；后面也可以接人：You can rely on me（你可以指望我）。
cards.example: Many small shops rely on tourists in the summer.

cards.note: to sleep well for the whole night
cards.tip: night's 带撇号 s，表示「一晚的」；动词也可以用 have。
cards.example: Try to get a good night's sleep before the interview.

cards.note: to slowly increase in amount or strength
cards.tip: 也能带宾语：build up your strength（慢慢增强体力）；build 的过去式是 built。
cards.example: If you don't reply to emails, they just build up.

cards.note: to start talking about a subject
动词词组是 cut off（切断）；名词带连字符。
to make time, money or space available for something else
来自意大利语，读 /ˈlɑːteɪ/ 或 /ˈlæteɪ/。
